title: TASER: Task-Aware Stein Regularisation for Geometry-Driven Smoothness
abstract: arXiv:2605.30601v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Deep neural networks remain sensitive to distribution shifts, motivating regularisation informed by data geometry. We introduce TASER (Task-Aware Stein Regularisation), a compact training-time framework that couples model derivatives to density scores by penalising the Langevin Stein operator. We establish a weighted Sobolev interpretation and a hierarchy of stability bounds under progressively stronger distributional assumptions. Moreover we introduce TASERLight, which is based on a first-order Stein operator. TASER and TASERLight require neither explicit tangent-space estimation nor an inner perturbation search. Controlled synthetic examples illustrate their effects on extrapolation and directional sensitivity. Experiments on spectroscopy, skeleton motion, ECG, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 demonstrate gains under distribution shift and complementary benefits when combined with isotropic regularisation.

translated_title: TASER：面向几何驱动平滑性的任务感知Stein正则化
translated_abstract: 深度神经网络对分布偏移仍然敏感，这促使人们寻求基于数据几何的正则化方法。我们提出了TASER（任务感知Stein正则化），这是一个紧凑的训练时框架，通过惩罚Langevin Stein算子将模型导数与密度得分耦合起来。我们建立了加权Sobolev解释，并在逐渐增强的分布假设下给出了一系列层次化的稳定性界。此外，我们还提出了基于一阶Stein算子的TASERLight。TASER和TASERLight既不需要显式的切空间估计，也不需要内层扰动搜索。受控的合成示例说明了它们对外推能力和方向敏感性的影响。在光谱学、骨骼运动、心电图（ECG）、MNIST和CIFAR-10数据集上的实验表明，该方法在分布偏移下带来了性能提升，并且与各向同性正则化结合时具有互补收益。
tldr: TASER通过惩罚Langevin Stein算子将模型导数与数据密度得分耦合，提出了一种无需切空间估计或内层扰动搜索的几何驱动正则化框架，有效提升深度神经网络在分布偏移下的稳定性与泛化能力。
en_tdlr: TASER couples model derivatives to density scores by penalising the Langevin Stein operator, providing a geometry-driven regularisation framework that improves deep neural network robustness under distribution shift without requiring tangent-space estimation or inner perturbation search.
